name: Montelukast + Levocetirizine
meta: Montelukast Sodium: Leukotriene receptor antagonist; Levocetirizine Dihydrochloride: Second-generation H1 antihistamine
Montelukast Sodium: R03DC03; Levocetirizine Dihydrochloride: R06AE09
Schedule H – prescription only; Levocetirizine Dihydrochloride: Schedule H – prescription only
sections: Hygroscopic, optically active, white to off-white powder (sodium), freely soluble in water.
White crystalline powder (dihydrochloride), freely soluble in water.

Montelukast Sodium: Generic since 2012. A US FDA boxed warning (March 2020) highlights serious neuropsychiatric events. First approval/introduction: US FDA 1998 (Merck & Co.). Levocetirizine Dihydrochloride: The active R-enantiomer of cetirizine (parent hydroxyzine family patented 1965); OTC in the USA since 2017. First approval/introduction: Launched 2001 (UCB, Europe); US FDA 2007.

Levocetirizine blocks histamine-mediated sneezing, itching and rhinorrhoea; montelukast blocks leukotriene-driven nasal congestion and airway inflammation – complementary control of early and late allergic responses.

Montelukast Sodium Selectively blocks the cysteinyl leukotriene CysLT1 receptor in airway and nasal mucosa, reducing bronchoconstriction, mucosal oedema, mucus secretion and eosinophilic inflammation. Receptor / target profile: Selective, high-affinity antagonist of the cysteinyl leukotriene CysLT1 receptor (LTD4).

Levocetirizine Dihydrochloride Active R-enantiomer of cetirizine; potent selective peripheral H1 receptor antagonist with anti-allergic and mild anti-inflammatory effects (reduces eosinophil migration). Receptor / target profile: Selective peripheral H1 inverse agonist with ~2-fold higher affinity than cetirizine (Ki ~3 nM); minimal CNS penetration.
Summary: Bioavailability ~64%; Tmax 3–4 h. >99% protein bound. Metabolised by CYP2C8, 3A4, 2C9. Half-life 2.7–5.5 h.
Summary: Rapid absorption; Tmax ~0.9 h. ~90% protein bound. Minimal metabolism; excreted unchanged in urine. Half-life ~8 h.
Allergic rhinitis (seasonal and perennial) – sneezing, rhinorrhoea, nasal congestion, itching
Adults and adolescents ≥15 years: one tablet once daily in the evening
Children: use paediatric strengths (montelukast 4–5 mg + levocetirizine 2.5 mg)
Dose to be individualised by the treating physician according to clinical response and tolerability.
Mild–moderate: no adjustment; severe: not studied.
6 months–5 years: 4 mg; 6–14 years: 5 mg; ≥15 years: 10 mg.
Can be used if clearly needed.
Levocetirizine Dihydrochloride Renal impairment                  CrCl 50–79: 5 mg daily; 30–49: 5 mg every 2 days; 10–29: 5 mg twice weekly; <10: contraindicated.
6 months–5 years: 1.25 mg daily; 6–11 years: 2.5 mg daily.
Hypersensitivity to levocetirizine, cetirizine or piperazine derivatives
Neuropsychiatric events (agitation, sleep disturbance, depression, suicidal thoughts) – boxed warning; counsel patients
Eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis (rare) on steroid tapering
Somnolence in some patients – caution driving
Urinary retention risk (spinal injury, prostatic hyperplasia)
Pruritus on discontinuation after long-term use
Montelukast Sodium: With or without food; evening dosing.
Levocetirizine Dihydrochloride: With or without food; avoid alcohol.
Montelukast Sodium: Thirst, somnolence, abdominal pain, hyperkinesia; supportive care. Levocetirizine Dihydrochloride: Drowsiness (adults); agitation then drowsiness (children). Supportive care.
Randomised trials (mainly Asian) show greater improvement in nasal symptoms, especially congestion, than levocetirizine alone in allergic rhinitis.
Not a rescue inhaler – keep reliever for attacks
Store below 30°C in a dry place, protected from light and moisture. Keep out of the reach of children. Do not use after the expiry date.
